html:
Chavín de Huántar is an ancient temple complex in the highlands of north-central Peru, built in stages from about 1200 BCE. It was the centre of the Chavín culture, whose religion and art spread across much of Peru.

The temple sits where two rivers meet, between the coast and the Amazon. Inside are dark stone passages, and at their centre stands the Lanzón, a carved stone image of a fanged god. Water channels under the temple may have made a roaring sound. Priests used drugs from the San Pedro cactus, as carvings show, and stone heads on the walls show men turning into jaguars.

Pilgrims came from far away, and Chavín styles appear in textiles and pottery across Peru, a first shared culture in the Andes, later followed by Paracas on the coast. It became a World Heritage Site in 1985. A mudslide buried part of it in 1945, in the same region later struck by the Ancash earthquake of 1970.
sum: Chavín de Huántar is an ancient temple complex in the highlands of north-central Peru, built in stages from about 1200 BCE. It was the centre of the Chavín culture, whose religion and art spread across much of Peru.
